summary: Round 5. The three claimed fixes are VERIFIED against the staged bytes: the 'Refusing neither duplicates nor suppresses' sentence is gone from the ADR (grep finds no remnant anywhere in the file); Consequences now reads 'so one GET answers a replay THE POINTED DELTA CARRIES ... a replay below the watermark need not be in it'; M4.10d's row carries the answer-or-refuse bound and its notes assign the refusal's caller semantics to M4.10d with the two-histories reason; and the ADR-0033 amendment paragraph names the pointer as well as the incarnation. Every factual claim I spot-checked in the ADR holds against the tree: Checkpoint.decode:151 is a strict version equality; CheckpointWriter:129 is pods.merge(podId, flushSeq, Math::max) and its javadoc:105 is 'the only place the writer can see podId and flushSeq'; DefaultIngest:349 evaluates flushSeq++ as the argument, so a throwing commit has already consumed it; ChainReplay:50 is the 'never GET at all' Hop javadoc; SegmentKey.MAX_KEY_BYTES is 1024; CheckpointTest:169 asserts < 64 KiB at 1,600 streams; the M3.0 quotation resolves in backlog-done.md:93. The decision itself now hangs together. What blocks is not the decision but its BLAST RADIUS: the commit chased the documents ADR-0036 falsifies for ADR-0033 and for M4.10d, and missed the two that actually direct the next sessions -- the M4 milestone SPEC, whose acceptance criterion 6 now MANDATES the harm this ADR exists to prevent, and M4.10c's notes, which still tell the session that picks it that the row is possibly void and prescribes nothing.

findings.title: The milestone SPEC's acceptance criterion 6 now mandates the exact harm ADR-0036 exists to prevent, and no part of this commit amends or assigns it (sdd.md rule 8)
findings.failure_scenario: M4/SPEC.md:415 states acceptance criterion 6 as: 'Commit is idempotent: replaying a `(podId, flushSeq)` already applied assigns no new offsets and returns the original assignment -- including when the replay arrives after a checkpoint recorded `lastAppliedFlushSeq`.' ADR-0036 makes that sentence false in the dangerous direction, twice. (a) A restarted pod reissuing flushSeq 0 IS 'a (podId, flushSeq) already applied', and the ADR decides it MUST be accepted and assigned new offsets; the criterion as written requires it to be suppressed, which is the ADR's own stated primary harm ('suppress real commits -- worse than the duplication it exists to prevent', ADR-0036:13-14). (b) 'returns the original assignment' is now unconditional in the SPEC and conditional in the ADR: ADR-0036:60-69 answers only when the pointed delta carries the exact triple and REFUSES otherwise, precisely because returning the pointed delta's offsets 'would hand back another flush's firstOffset'. Concretely: a session implements M4.10d, reads criterion 6 as the binding acceptance criterion (it is the milestone's, and M4.15 is the row that verifies it), keys dedup on the pair to satisfy 'replaying a (podId, flushSeq) already applied assigns no new offsets', and ships suppression of real commits with every gate and the milestone review green -- or, satisfying the second half literally, returns the pointed delta's offsets for a non-matching replay. The same falsification stands at SPEC.md:147-148 (scope item 9, '`(podId, flushSeq)` with `lastAppliedFlushSeq` per pod, carried in checkpoints'), :55 and :503 (the commit request carries `(podId, flushSeq, segments...)`, which ADR-0036:38-39 changes by adding incarnationId to CommitRequest), :468 (the T0 test-tier row) and :513. sdd.md rule 8 -- selected for this diff -- says a spec that turns out to be wrong is AMENDED, not worked around, and the tree already cites that rule for exactly this situation: backlog M4.8b1 rejects an alternative because 'the M4 SPEC states the ... grammar NORMATIVELY and changing it means amending the SPEC in the same commit under sdd.md rule 8'. This commit demonstrates it knows the move -- it amended ADR-0033's header -- and then did not apply it to the document that carries the milestone's checkable criteria. Remedy is cheap and can be either: a dated amendment banner on criteria 6 and 9 in SPEC.md pointing at ADR-0036 and stating that a same-pair replay from a DIFFERENT incarnation must be accepted and that answering is conditional on the pointed delta; or, if the SPEC is to be amended by whoever implements, one paragraph in ADR-0036 naming criterion 6 and scope item 9 as amended and one clause in M4.10c/d's rows owning the edit. What is not acceptable is the current state, where an accepted ADR and the milestone's acceptance criteria say opposite things and neither points at the other.

findings.title: M4.10c's row was rewritten to prescribe the shape; M4.10c's NOTES were not touched and still discredit that prescription -- and the notes are what the session that picks the row is told to read
findings.failure_scenario: The diff rewrites the M4.10c row (backlog.md) from 'CONDITIONAL ON M4.10b AND POSSIBLY VOID: ONLY the format change, if that ADR needs one' to 'CARRY THE IDEMPOTENCY TRIPLE IN BOTH FORMATS, per ADR-0036 ... CommitDelta carries the triple PER SegmentCommit, not once per delta'. The notes section that row links to (#m410c) is unchanged and still opens '⚠️ CONDITIONAL ON M4.10b AND POSSIBLY VOID', then says 'If a field is needed, CommitDelta and Checkpoint must agree on the key's SHAPE', and -- the harmful one -- '⚠️ THE TWO DISCRIMINATE DIFFERENTLY AND THIS ROW DOES NOT PRESCRIBE HOW; two earlier drafts did, wrongly.' AGENTS.md tells a session to read the notes for the ONE task it picks, so the next session to pick M4.10c is handed a row that prescribes the placement and an essay saying this row deliberately does not prescribe it and that previous attempts to prescribe were wrong. Concretely: the session resolves the contradiction in favour of the notes (they are longer, they are the stated reasoning, and they explicitly warn against prescriptions), decides placement for itself, and puts the triple once per delta -- which ADR-0036:99-103 says round-trips, passes both new goldens and is byte-equivalent today because every M4 delta is single-segment, and drops every pod but one on M5's first forwarded multi-pod batch. That is an M4-invisible defect with no test that can fail, chosen by following the notes the row points at. The same commit updated M4.10d's notes in exactly this way and left its sibling; the immediately preceding commit's own staged baselines entry names this failure class ('AND DELETING THE SECTION MISSED ITS DUPLICATE: the same facts sat inside the M4.10 row ... fixing one copy of a fact and missing its duplicates'). Also unfixed in the same family, and cheaper to fix in the same pass: the parent M4.10 row (backlog.md:122, still an open row) says 'commit idempotency on `(podId, flushSeq)`' and 'c is conditional on that and may be void', both falsified by this commit; the M4.10 notes section repeats 'M4.10c happens only if it does, and may be void'.

findings.title: The falsified claim survives in PRODUCTION javadoc, with no row owning the correction
findings.failure_scenario: CommitRequest's class javadoc says '`(podId, flushSeq)` is the idempotency key M4.10 will use to ignore a replay', and its @param flushSeq says 'Together with `podId` it identifies this commit uniquely across the fleet' -- the precise premise ADR-0036 kills, sitting on the record ADR-0036:38-39 says must carry the incarnation. Failure scenario: a session implementing M4.10c reads the record it is about to widen, sees its contract asserting the pair is fleet-unique, and keeps the CommitRequest-level contract as-is while widening only the persisted formats -- so the seam that M5 forwards over still documents the bare pair as the key. This is the M4.42 pattern (a corrected claim surviving in two duplicates, one of them in production) reproduced one commit later. No fix is needed in this docs-only commit; what is missing is an owner. One clause in M4.10c's or M4.10d's row naming CommitRequest's javadoc closes it deterministically.

findings.title: The cost paragraph still accounts only for detection; RECORD it rather than spend another round on it
findings.failure_scenario: 'No commit-path request scales with pods. Detection is an in-memory comparison against state recovered once per takeover.' The paragraph above it (:60-69) puts one GET on the commit path per DETECTED replay, and the slot is per pod pointing at that pod's own last-applied delta -- so the pointers of B replaying pods are B DISTINCT objects, uncoalescable. After a takeover, the moment ADR-0036:105-107 itself calls 'when duplicates are likeliest', a correlated retry across the fleet costs one GET per replaying pod; and if M4.10d's caller semantics retry on a refusal, the loop is one GET per retry per pod, sustained, since the ADR names no cache and the pointed delta is immutable. I am NOT escalating this: pods are nodes, and cost.md's invariant explicitly PERMITS a rate that scales with nodes -- the stricter 'no commit-path request scales with pods' is the task row's own constraint, aimed at M4.7's steady-state PUT multiplication, and this GET is zero in steady state and bursty rather than sustained. So: record it in the commit body per review.md rule minors-land. If it is ever fixed, the honest form is one clause on that paragraph ('detection is free; answering costs one GET per detected replay') plus a line in M4.10d's notes bounding the retry-on-refusal loop -- not a rewrite.

findings.title: Two arguments rest on the incarnationId being a UUID; the Decision never makes that normative
findings.failure_scenario: The Decision (:36-39) says only 'minted once per INGESTER process'. Consequences then leans on UUID-ness twice: ':137-138' sizes the checkpoint at '16 bytes as a UUID', and ':160-161' discharges the ADR-0031 scenario with 'Two such processes would share an incarnationId only by minting collision, which a UUID makes negligible without coordination'. Checkpoint's existing encoding is uvarint-based end to end (Checkpoint.java:137), so the cheap thing for M4.10c to reach for is a uvarint -- and a low-entropy per-process value (a coarse start-timestamp, a monotonic counter seeded at 0, a value derived from the epoch) satisfies 'minted once per process' while two cold-started pods with the same podId mint the same one, which re-opens the exact suppression the ADR is written to close, with every seam test green because those tests supply the incarnation. Make the entropy requirement normative in the Decision (a UUID, or 'at least 64 random bits, minted without coordination'), or drop the two arguments that depend on it. Minor because a competent implementer reaches for a UUID; recorded because both of the ADR's supporting arguments become unsupported if they do not.
